name: MN3005
description: 4096-stage bucket-brigade delay line, the long-delay member of the MN3000 series, 4x the stage count of the MN3007. Variable analog delay of 20.48-204.8ms. The classic long-delay BBD used in the Electro-Harmonix Deluxe Memory Man and many other analog delay pedals. Needs an external clock generator to drive CP1/CP2.

pins.name: VDD
pins.description: negative supply (typically -15V referenced to GND in the classic bias scheme)

pins.name: VGG
pins.description: bias supply, a few volts above VDD (see datasheet bias network) -- still negative relative to GND (VDD=-15V, VGG=VDD+1~=-14V), not a VCC/ground-referenced positive rail

DIP-8.notes: Per Panasonic's own block diagram/pinout, DIP-8, top view. This is Panasonic's 'special' 8-lead DIP outline for the MN3005; the pin FUNCTION order differs from the MN3007's DIP-8 (e.g. IN is pin 7 here, pin 3 on the MN3007), despite both being 8-pin DIPs -- do not assume the two are pin-compatible.

extra.clock_range: 10 to 100kHz (matches the 20.48-204.8ms delay range: delay = stages / (2 x clock))
extra.supply: VDD=-15V, VGG=VDD+1 (per Panasonic's bias scheme; see application notes for the exact bias network)

typical_application: Long analog delay/echo effects (100+ ms) in guitar pedals and electronic musical instruments; the classic chip in vintage analog delay units. Requires an external clock and a low-pass anti-aliasing filter on the output.
gotchas: pin arrangement is NOT the same as the MN3007 despite both being 8-pin DIPs; check the pin list here, don't assume cross-compatibility
needs an external clock generator driving CP1/CP2 with complementary, non-overlapping phases; it is not self-clocking
delay time is inversely proportional to clock frequency: higher clock = shorter delay, lower clock = longer delay (and worse bandwidth/noise)
clock feedthrough onto the output is normal and expected; always follow with a low-pass filter tuned below the clock frequency

genuine NOS Panasonic/Matsushita chips are increasingly scarce and sought after (this is THE Deluxe Memory Man chip); some modern builds substitute other MN3xxx-family or clone BBD chips with similar but not identical specs

read from a genuine Panasonic factory datasheet (clear letterhead, block diagram, and package drawing), but no current live-hosted URL was found for this decades-old scan; datasheet_url is left blank rather than citing a secondhand mirror
